variables.values: Integer N parsed with std::atol. N <= 0 turns hardware (FPGA) attention off for all models; non-numeric text parses as 0. N > 0 turns it on for all eligible models and also sets the engagement point.
variables.default: Unset: each model uses its compiled default, and the engagement point is token position 127. The default is on when the model plugin defines force_hw_attn = true and off otherwise; the ingest code generator emits that constant (ingest/src/TronCpp.hs:258). An empty value parses as 0, which is off for all models.
variables.effect: Selects whether attention runs on the FPGA cards or in software. With N > 0 it also sets the first 0-based token position of a sequence that hardware attention serves; software serves all positions below it.
variables.notes: Engagement point for N > 0: N is capped at 2^30, then pages = (N + 128) / 128 by integer division, and the point is max(127, pages * 128 - 1). So N from 1 to 127 gives 127 and N = 128 gives 255. The value is read once per process. The variable cannot force hardware attention: the model shape, an EAGLE draft model, a missing POS device, the capacity of EMEM (the FPGA memory that holds the Q.K dot products) and the activation format each keep a model in software (h/tron/models/model.hpp:769-786 and :1803-1818). There are 14 reader lines in this area; 6 are listed. The other 8 are helper calls: hw_attn_engagement_point at h/tron/models/model.hpp:1864, :2966, :3065, :3067 and h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2110, and use_hw_attn_for_this_model at h/tron/models/model.hpp:1817, :2891 and h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2151. h/runtron/stream_generate.hpp:863 (outside this area) also calls hw_attn_engagement_point().

variables.effect: Sets the soft limit on the number of live tokens (token jobs) that one forward pass of a scheduler takes. At the limit the scheduler stops adding tokens to the pass and records that the pass did not schedule everything.
variables.notes: When the model config has max_minibatches above 0, the limit is lowered to max_minibatches x max_minibatch_size. The field comment calls it a soft limit that can be exceeded in some cases (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:1976): a page that already has KV work is bound only by the hard capacity limit. The variable is read each time a scheduler is constructed. The code does not reject 0.

variables.name: TRON_LATCH_WATCHDOG

readers.program: model code in h/tron/models (compiled into the model objects of the full scheduler library: rinzler, runtron, rinzler_host, tests), constructor of tron::latch_arena in h/tron/threading.hpp
readers.mechanism: std::getenv; the pointer is kept in a function-local static

setters.why: Workflow-level env block. The comment says the watchdog is polled every 60 seconds.

variables.values: Integer parsed with std::atoi. A non-zero value turns the watchdog on. 0 or non-numeric text leaves it off. The unit is seconds between log outputs.
variables.default: Off when unset or empty.
variables.effect: Each latch arena starts a watchdog thread. Every N seconds the thread writes an info log entry 'Latch states' with the count and name of every latch in the arena.
variables.notes: A latch is a counter that threads wait on during a forward pass; each model state owns one latch arena (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1240). The watchdog thread pins itself to CPU 0 and wakes every 100 ms. The environment is read once; the text is converted again for each new arena. The code does not reject a negative value.

variables.name: TRON_SPEEDOMETER_TIMESCALE

readers.program: libtron (static library tron, linked into rinzler, runtron and the other TRON binaries), constructor of tron::speedometer_t in h/tron/threading.hpp
readers.when: every call of the speedometer_t constructor

variables.values: Floating-point number parsed with std::atof. It must be above 0. The unit is update steps of the estimator.
variables.default: 10.0 when unset. An empty value parses as 0 and the process aborts.
variables.effect: Sets the time constant of the per-worker speed estimator. Old measurements are scaled by exp(-1 / value) at each update, so a larger value makes the estimate change more slowly.
variables.notes: The speed estimates split attention work between the attention workers (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2433). They are not used when the model config has pay_for_determinism set. The variable is read each time a thread pool is constructed; the shared pool is created on first use (h/tron/threading.hpp:755). A value of 0 or below, or non-numeric text, fails TRON_ASSERT_GT at h/tron/threading.hpp:528 and the process aborts.

variables.name: TRON_SPEEDOMETER_PRIOR_STRENGTH

readers.program: libtron (static library tron, linked into rinzler, runtron and the other TRON binaries), constructor of tron::speedometer_t in h/tron/threading.hpp
readers.when: every call of the speedometer_t constructor

variables.values: Floating-point number parsed with std::atof. It must be 0 or above. It is a ratio without unit. Non-numeric text gives 0.
variables.default: 0.1 when unset. An empty value gives 0.
variables.effect: Sets how strongly each worker's speed estimate is pulled toward the mean of all workers at each update. The factor is exp(-value / timescale); 0 removes the pull.
variables.notes: The speed estimates split attention work between the attention workers (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2433). They are not used when the model config has pay_for_determinism set. The variable is read each time a thread pool is constructed; the shared pool is created on first use (h/tron/threading.hpp:755). A negative value fails TRON_ASSERT_GE at h/tron/threading.hpp:529 and the process aborts. The timescale is TRON_SPEEDOMETER_TIMESCALE or its default.

variables.name: TRON_LOG_PLACEMENT

readers.program: libtron (static library tron, linked into rinzler, runtron and the other TRON binaries), constructor of tron::hardware::placement_context
readers.when: every call of the placement_context constructor

variables.values: Any value turns it on, including an empty value. The text is not parsed.
variables.default: Off when unset.
variables.effect: Each placement context counts, per tensor name and per device, how many tiles it placed. It writes the counts as JSON in one info log line 'Tensor device counts' when the context is destroyed.
variables.notes: A placement context exists while model weights are placed on the FPGA cards, for example during a model load (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1028).

variables.name: POS_WEIGHTS_DIR

readers.program: libtron (static library tron, linked into rinzler, runtron and the other TRON binaries), tron::resolve_weights
libtron header h/tron/models/registry.hpp, tron::default_model_weights

setters.why: Checks that a relative model name resolves under this directory.
Checks that a changed value is used by the next call.
Checks that an empty value selects the default root.
Used by a further test case.

variables.values: Path to a directory.
variables.default: /opt/positron/weights/huggingface when unset or empty.
variables.effect: Sets the root directory under which a relative model weights name, such as <org>/<model>, is looked up. The found path is made canonical once.
variables.notes: An absolute weights path does not use the variable. When the directory is missing, the function logs an error and returns an empty path; default_model_weights then aborts with 'Couldn't find weights directory' (h/tron/models/registry.hpp:95). The variable is read on each call, so a change during the run affects later lookups. t/t_prequant_cache.cpp sets the variable at 5 sites in total; line 435 is not listed.

variables.name: TRON_GOLDEN_TOKENS

readers.program: rinzler_proxy (proxy_scheduler library), tron::proxy::load_golden_map_from_env
rinzler_proxy (proxy_scheduler library), stream_generate

setters.why: Environment of the rinzler_proxy process that the Python launcher starts.
Environment of the rinzler_proxy child process that the test starts.
In-process test of the loader.
Test fixture that points the loader at its file.

variables.values: Path to a JSON file (the golden map). The file maps a prompt, written as a comma-separated list of token ids, to the tokens that the proxy must emit. It may hold a default entry and a rendered_at date.
variables.default: Unset: the loader logs an error, and every generation throws std::runtime_error 'proxy: golden map unavailable'. An empty value is tried as a file name and fails in the same way.
variables.effect: Names the file from which rinzler_proxy takes its output tokens. Generation in rinzler_proxy emits these scripted tokens instead of running a model (README.proxy.md:19).
variables.notes: The variable and the file are read again for every generation, so the file can change while the proxy runs. A file that cannot be read, is not JSON, or has a wrong shape gives the same per-request error. The file format is described at h/tron/scheduler/golden_tokens.hpp:102 and in README.proxy.md. t/t_rinzler_proxy.cpp sets the variable at 9 sites in total. rinzler_proxy is a stand-in for rinzler that is used for tests (README.proxy.md:21).

variables.name: RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE

readers.program: rinzler_proxy (proxy_scheduler library), tron::proxy::golden_map::validate_rendered_at
rinzler_proxy (proxy_scheduler library), stream_generate

setters.value: the rendered_at value of the golden file
setters.why: Environment of the rinzler_proxy process, so that the date matches the capture.

setters.value: the rendered_at value of the golden file
setters.why: Environment of the rinzler_proxy child process that the test starts.

variables.values: Date text. This reader compares it, character by character, with the rendered_at entry of the golden file. It does not parse the date.
variables.default: Unset: when the golden file has a rendered_at entry, the generation throws std::runtime_error. When the file has no rendered_at entry, the variable is not read here.
variables.effect: In rinzler_proxy, a generation is refused unless the value equals the rendered_at date stored in the golden file. This check makes sure that prompts are rendered with the date that was used when the file was captured.
variables.notes: This entry covers only the read in the proxy scheduler. The main reader is rinzler, which validates the format YYYY-MM-DD at startup (src/rinzler/harmony.cpp:892, outside this area). The check runs for every generation, before the prompt key is looked up. An empty value differs from any date, so it also throws.

wrappers.description: Reads TRON_PER_USER_PROMPT_CHUNK_LIMIT with std::getenv once and caches the result. Returns the prompt chunk size in tokens (default 128).
Reads TRON_NO_PREQUANT_CACHE on every call. Returns true for any non-empty value other than 0. Called only by t/t_prequant_cache.cpp at this commit.
Reads POS_PREQUANT_CACHE, then POS_WEIGHTS_CACHE, on every call. Returns the root directory of the prequant cache. Reached only from t/t_prequant_cache.cpp at this commit.
Reads TRON_ATTN_STATS once and caches the result. Returns true only for exactly the text 1; warns once for any other set value.
Reads TRON_LOG_KV_GRANULARITY once (bytes, default 1 GiB) and uses it as the step between 'KV cache footprint' log lines.
Reads TRON_MIN_MAIN_HELPERS with getenv on every call (no cache). Returns the minimum number of main helper threads.
Reads TRON_MAX_MAIN_HELPERS with getenv on every call (no cache). Returns the maximum number of main helper threads.
Reads TRON_MAX_LOGITS_CHUNK_SIZE once and caches min(value, pool workers).
Reads TRON_HWATTN_EARLY_LAUNCH_MIN_B once and caches it (default 4). Aborts on a value that is not a positive integer.
Reads TRON_ATTN_SECTION_SPLIT once and caches min(value, 16) (default 8). Aborts on a value that is not a nonnegative integer.
Reads USE_HW_ATTN once and caches two results: the on/off override (empty when unset) and the engagement point.
Returns the USE_HW_ATTN on/off override from parsed_hw_attn_env, or the caller's default when the variable is unset.
Returns the first token position served by hardware attention, from parsed_hw_attn_env (USE_HW_ATTN); 127 by default.
Calls fwd_hw_attn_enabled (USE_HW_ATTN) after two hardware checks that the variable cannot override.
Reads TRON_DEFRAG_BOOKS_DEPTH once and caches it (default 0, off).
Reads TRON_BOOK_MAX_TOKENS once and caches max(1, value) (default 1600 tokens).
Reads TRON_BOOK_INITIAL_TOKENS once and caches max(1, value) (default 1600 tokens).
Reads TRON_BOOK_GROWTH_FACTOR once and caches max(1.0, value) (default 2.0).
Reads TRON_PERF_INTERVAL_SEC once (seconds, default 0 = off) and uses it as the interval between throughput log lines.
Caches the result of detect_and_request (src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:85), which reads TRON_AMX_DISABLE and probes the CPU. Returns false when the variable is exactly 1.
Reads POS_WEIGHTS_DIR on every call for a relative weights name. get_weights_path (src/tron/models/load.cpp:59) and default_model_weights (h/tron/models/registry.hpp:91) call it.
Reads TRON_GOLDEN_TOKENS on every call and loads the JSON file it names.
Reads RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE on every call when the golden map has a rendered_at entry. Throws when the two differ.

notes: Coverage. All 162 files of the area were searched with these patterns: getenv (any spelling), environ, envp, setenv, putenv, unsetenv, clearenv, load_env; every identifier that contains env; exec, spawn, popen, fork and system calls; quoted upper-case names with the prefixes TRON, POS, RZ, DICE, HWATTN, USE and common system names; unquoted upper-case names with the TRON_, POS_, RZ_ prefixes; library calls that read the environment indirectly (temp_directory_path, locale, hwloc, curl, httplib). The code around every hit was read. Files without a hit were not read line by line. Result: 34 getenv call lines in 14 files, 31 distinct variables, all with role read. The area files contain no setenv, putenv, exec or spawn call, so there is no set_only entry. No name is built at run time. Helpers named in the scope hint that are NOT in this area: read_arena_allocator_env (src/system/memory.cpp:93), read_heap_shadow_env (src/system/memory.cpp:106), hwattn_env_override (src/pos/device.cpp:102) and rtm_disabled_by_env (src/system/mwaitx.cpp:40) are static functions in files outside the area list, and no area file calls them. Their variables are left to the areas that own those files. RZ_KV_CACHE_GB is not read in this area. src/tron/scheduler/token_cache_control.cpp:86 only prints the name in a warning: when the arena allocator is active, the static KV cache sizing knobs (RZ_KV_CACHE_GB, --kv-cache-gb, --kv-cache-bytes) are ignored. The read is at src/rinzler.cpp:4575. Area files call system-layer functions whose environment reads are in other areas, for example hardware::system::system_init (h/tron/generation/harvester.hpp:369) and hardware::system::get_kv_cache_size (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache.cpp:455). These are not listed here. src/tronutil.cpp uses cpp-httplib with OpenSSL to reach huggingface.co. The file itself reads no environment variable; any variable that those libraries read was not determined from the checkout and is not listed. Names in the area that look like variables but are C preprocessor macros or CMake options, and are therefore not listed: TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, TRON_PAGE_SHARE_COUNTERS, TRON_MWAIT_STATS, TRON_ENABLE_SESSION_REPORTING, TRON_IGNORE_NAN, TRON_IGNORE_FTZ, TRON_SCHEDULER_RUNTIME_ONLY, TRON_CHUNK_SIZE. Audience choices that a reviewer may want to change: the three prequant cache variables are marked test, because only t/t_prequant_cache.cpp runs the reader at this commit; TRON_ATTN_STATS, TRON_PERF_INTERVAL_SEC and the two TRON_SPEEDOMETER variables are marked operator (statistics, logging, tuning) and could also be seen as developer-debug. Existing documentation found during the sweep: h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:50 says that TRON_AMX_DISABLE 'will be listed in the TRON environment-variable document' and cites https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/issues/4338. README.stats.md describes TRON_ATTN_STATS. README.proxy.md:278 describes TRON_GOLDEN_TOKENS. doc/model_manifest.md section 9 describes POS_WEIGHTS_DIR, POS_WEIGHTS_CACHE and POS_PREQUANT_CACHE. The setter sites listed in the entries are outside this area (tests, scripts, one workflow); they were found with git grep over the whole checkout and each line was read.
